chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from Harun ibn Muslim from Mas'adah ibn Sadah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard my father (peace be upon him) saying: 'When the owner of the net strikes with the net, whatever living or dead creature it catches therein is permissible, except that which has no shell and the floating fish that is not eaten.'

Because this report is construed to mean that the living and the dead are permissible for him if they are not distinguished for him; as for when they are distinguished, it is not permissible to eat that which died in it, according to what we have previously stated.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on eating fish or animals caught in a net?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), transmitted via his father Imam al-Baqir (AS), clarifies the permissibility of consuming net-caught game by distinguishing between general permissibility and specific exclusions like shellless creatures and floating fish. The juristic reasoning highlights the principle of 'istishab' (presumption of continuity) where undifferentiated catch is treated as permissible, whereas distinguished catch follows the rule of 'mawat' (dead by drowning) if not slaughtered. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for understanding the conditions under which aquatic animals become halal without ritual slaughter.
